Finding concentration round (triage seat, session `session_01Kktexqp6uVuFMztvvTMf3V`, 2026-08-24, maintainer-invoked): promoted → `pm:queue` (`domain:ui`), Task. Converge the four restatements (kanban, detail ×2, resolveActionParams) onto `EXPANDABLE_FIELD_TYPES` and pin each against the canonical set — each site also gains the `user`/`tree` members it is missing and sheds the undeclarable `reference` special-casing per the family's canonical home. **Fold candidate with #5875** (the false "fourth and last" claims — one PR can fix the copies AND the claim); ui seat answers fold-or-serial in the chain-head claim.

## ⛔ FOLD RULING — triage asked the ui seat to answer fold-or-serial; the answer is **FOLD**

Triage, 2026-08-24: *"**Fold candidate with #5875** (the false 'fourth and last' claims — one PR can fix the copies AND the claim); ui seat answers fold-or-serial in the chain-head claim."*

**Folded.** Five gates, answered:

① **Same defect shape — and tighter than usual.** #5875's false claim is *about the very copies* #5874 converges. Fixing the copies **changes the count the claim states**, so landing #5874 alone leaves `paramToField.ts` asserting "fourth and last" while the true answer has just moved again — wrong a second time, in the file the next consolidation reads first. ⭐ That is not a coincidence of timing; it is the same defect at two levels (the copies, and the record of how many there are).
② **One changeset**, one family, one canonical home.
③ Both graded `pm:queue` / Task in the **same** 2026-08-24 concentration round; neither is in the decision box.
④ Independently checkable — #5874 by identity pins, #5875 by grep on the prose.
⑤ **Exclusion list:** #5692 is landed (it corrected the canonical home); **#5654** is a *different* rule (degraded-hint, not reference-bearing) and stays out; #5312 / #4770 / #4790 / #4815 are prior landed sweeps. Neither card is claimed by another session.

**`Fixes #5874` and `Fixes #5875` both.**

## The convergence

`@object-ui/core`'s **`EXPANDABLE_FIELD_TYPES`** (`packages/core/src/utils/expand-fields.ts`) is the published reference-bearing field family. Four faces restate it inline, none deriving from it, none pinned against it:

| file | restatement |
|---|---|
| `plugin-kanban/src/ObjectKanban.tsx:346` | `lookup \|\| master_detail \|\| reference` |
| `plugin-detail/src/RecordDetailDrawer.tsx:227` | `lookup \|\| master_detail \|\| reference` |
| `plugin-detail/src/HeaderHighlight.tsx:147` | `reference \|\| lookup \|\| master_detail` (inside a wider `isWide` disjunction) |
| `app-shell/src/utils/resolveActionParams.ts:489` | `lookup \|\| reference` (⚠️ also omits `master_detail`) |

⭐ **Every one diverges in BOTH directions**, which is why this is not mere duplication:
- **`user` missing from all four** — it carries the same foreign-key storage as `lookup` and resolves through the same expand path (#2032 put it in the family). On these faces a `user` column is not treated as a relation.
- **`tree` missing from all four.**
- **`reference` present in all four, and no producer can emit it** — measured on #5692's branch against `@objectstack/spec`'s **closed** `FieldType` vocabulary, with `lookup`/`master_detail`/`user`/`tree` as live controls and retired `owner` plus a nonsense spelling as dead ones: `reference` is absent, and `FieldSchema.safeParse({ type: 'reference' })` is **refused**. It sits exactly where `owner` sat before #4814 retired it. **Dead weight that reads as live capability.**

**Shape:** read `EXPANDABLE_FIELD_TYPES` and carry an **identity pin** — a spy on its `.has` — so a member-identical private copy **fails rather than quietly re-forking**. ⛔ **Do NOT copy the set.** That instruction is the whole point of the family's five prior sweeps.

## The #5875 half

`packages/app-shell/src/utils/paramToField.ts` says *"This face held the **fourth and last** private copy of it"*; `paramToField.test.ts` says *"This module held the **FOURTH and last** hand-maintained answer to one question."* Both were true-as-measured when written and are now known false — there were at least six, and this card adds four more.

**Prose only, no behaviour.** Replace "fourth and last" with what is measured — this face was the fourth **converted**, not the last copy — and ⛔ **point at `expand-fields.ts`'s falsification note rather than restating a count locally.** ⭐ Hand-kept counts of this table are exactly what keeps going stale; the mechanical fact is the identity pins. ⚠️ **So do not write a new number.** If you write "the seventh and last", you have re-created the defect with a bigger integer.

## PM mechanism assumptions — measure, do not assume

1. **Both cards are from 2026-08-23 and four of the five files sit in packages this seat merged into today** (#6015/#6000 in `plugin-detail`, #6035 in `app-shell`, #6037 in `components`). ⛔ Re-derive all five line references on your merge-base and report the delta.
2. ⚠️ **"Each face needs its own call on whether gaining `user`/`tree` is the intended behaviour there."** The card says so and explicitly does not pre-empt it: *"on the four above it looks like restoration rather than widening, but that is a per-face judgement."* ✅ Make that call **per face, with the read site as evidence**. ⛔ If any face would be **widened** rather than restored by gaining `user`/`tree` — i.e. it would start treating as a relation something it deliberately does not — **stop and report that face** rather than converging it. Converging three and reporting one is a better outcome than converging four on an assumption.
3. ⚠️ **`resolveActionParams.ts:489` is the odd one — it omits `master_detail` too.** So it diverges on three members, not two. Treat it as its own judgement, not as "the same as the other three".
4. ⚠️ **`HeaderHighlight.tsx:147` sits inside a wider `isWide` disjunction.** Converging the reference-bearing part must not change what the *rest* of that disjunction decides. Measure the surrounding condition before touching it.
5. ⛔ **`ActionParamDialog.tsx:351` is NOT this card** — a different rule (degraded-hint), already filed as **#5654**. A sweep for the three-way disjunction will catch it; the sweep is wrong.

## Verification

**The identity pin is the deliverable.** A spy on `EXPANDABLE_FIELD_TYPES.has` per converged face, so a future hand-copy that happens to be member-identical still **fails**. ⛔ Asserting the resulting member set is not sufficient — that is exactly what let five prior sweeps re-fork.

Direction predicted **before** running: replace one converged face with a member-identical private copy and show its identity pin goes **red** (the member-set assertion will stay green — say so, that contrast is the proof the pin is doing work the set assertion cannot).

**Counter-probes required:** (a) a `user` field is now treated as reference-bearing on each converged face — the restoration half, which must be able to fail; (b) a field of a type genuinely outside the family is still **not** treated as reference-bearing — otherwise convergence is satisfiable by treating everything as a relation.

Prove every mutation on disk by grepping the injected text **and separately** the removed text; ⚠️ **print the landing site**, and ⚠️ **assert anchor uniqueness before writing** — ⚠️ especially here: **four of these five restatements are near-identical disjunctions**, which is the exact terrain where an anchor hits three sites (measured on #5927 today). Restore under `trap … EXIT INT TERM`, and ⚠️ **make the restore command cwd-independent** — a trap that fires is not a trap that restored (measured on #5926 today). Confirm `git diff HEAD --stat` empty afterwards.

Gates by name with exit codes: `type-check` for `plugin-kanban`, `plugin-detail`, `app-shell` (⚠️ hyphenated; echo the script name; distinguish the **unbuilt-closure** red from the **missing-`node_modules`** red — both were hit today), root-form vitest over each affected package's paths (⚠️ **app-shell path-filtered — whole-package vitest is ~784 s and holds the shared lock; ⛔ do not run it**; and the guard refuses `--filter` forms — use `pnpm exec vitest run <paths>` from the repo root), `node scripts/check-phantom-dependencies.mjs` if any package gains an import of `@object-ui/core`, and eslint on changed files with merge-base delta. ⚠️ Plain `eslint .` per package — ⛔ no `--no-inline-config`.

Changeset required. Draft PR, `Fixes #5874` **and** `Fixes #5875`. ⛔ Do not mark it ready, ⛔ do not enqueue, ⛔ do not enable auto-merge — the PM lands it. Post the terminal report here (plain-text first-line marker `os-dev-report`; ⛔ avoid short angle-bracket placeholders in prose — the sanitizer ate one on #5926 today) and return it.

## PM review — **ACCEPT** (both #5874 and #5875)

PR #6064, head `6e9bd1a9b`, merge-base `b65fe911d`. Gate read at the usual mark.

**Fences held, checked:** `packages/core/**` returns **nothing** in the diff — `expand-fields.ts`, the canonical home, is untouched. `ActionParamDialog.tsx` likewise untouched, so #5654's boundary held against a sweep that would naturally have caught it.

### ⭐ The best thing in this report: a pin that did not work, caught by its own ablation

> the kanban pin written as a bare `vi.spyOn(EXPANDABLE_FIELD_TYPES,'has').mock.calls` check **survived its own ablation 6/6 GREEN**, because `ObjectKanban.tsx` also imports `buildExpandFields`, which consults the same shared object once per schema field on every render — so **"some call happened" was satisfied by a face that never converged**.

You then **measured the stacks** (3 calls from `buildExpandFields`, 1 from `resolveDisplay`), rewrote the pin to filter recorded calls by calling frame, re-ran the ablation → **2 failed / 5 passed**.

✅ This is the entire reason the ablation requirement exists, demonstrated on itself. An identity pin that cannot fail is *worse* than no pin: it advertises a guarantee it does not provide, and it would have shipped green. ⛔ Nothing but running the ablation could have found it — the pin looked correct, the convergence *was* correct, and the two facts were unconnected.

✅ **And keeping the un-attributed version as a green-either-way test documenting why the filter is there** is the right disposition: the next person who "simplifies" the frame filter now trips over a test whose whole purpose is to say *this weaker form passes vacuously*.

⭐ **#6063 explains the harness failure, not just a defect.** `ObjectKanban`'s `resolveDisplay` guard is **unreachable** — `if (isLookup && isOpaqueId(raw)) return undefined;` is immediately followed by `if (isOpaqueId(raw)) return undefined;`, which subsumes it for every input. So **no membership delta on that face is observable in either direction** — which is *why* the first pin could not be falsified. ✅ And the test file **records that absence rather than writing a counter-probe that cannot fail** — declining to write a probe you know is vacuous is harder and better than writing one.

### `resolveActionParams` — the face that diverges twice, and where my dispatch was too broad

I told you `reference` is dead: *"no producer can emit it… `FieldSchema.safeParse({ type: 'reference' })` is refused."* On three faces that holds. On this one it does **not**, and you measured why:

> `reference` is refused by the spec's `ActionParamSchema` too, **but the dialog still ACCEPTS it** from params already authored with it via the `PARAM_TYPE_ALIASES` legacy dialect, so dropping the branch outright would have **silently degraded such a param to a text input**.

⛔ That is a real regression my "shed `reference`" instruction would have caused, avoided by not applying a family-level fact to a face without checking the face. ✅ And the resolution is better than a carve-out: the face asks the shared family **over the widget key the one alias table produces** — *deliberately the same expression `paramToField` evaluates one step later* — so **the half that populates a param's picker config and the half that forwards it can no longer disagree.** That is the convergence's actual purpose applied one level deeper than the card asked.

✅ Its second divergence (missing `master_detail` too — three members, not two) was correctly treated as its own judgement rather than "same as the other three", exactly as the dispatch required.

### Per-face judgement on `user`/`tree` — argued, not assumed

✅ **Restoration on all four**, each from the read site's **own stated reason**: the drawer has no relation picker, so a plain text input lets a user overwrite the relation with a free-form string — *as true of `user`/`tree` as of `lookup`*; the strip's picker needs the room, and the component's own `dataSource` prop doc **already names `lookup`/`user` together** as the reference editors; `resolveActionParams` without the picker config degrades to the #3405 paste-a-record-id box. ⛔ No face would have been widened, so none was stopped — and saying so explicitly closes the rule rather than leaving it silent.

✅ **`HeaderHighlight`'s wider `isWide` disjunction was measured before touching** — only the reference-bearing part moved, `email`/`url`/`textarea` preserved verbatim **and pinned both as still-wide and as still-NOT family members**. That second pin is the one that matters: it stops a future convergence quietly absorbing them.

### The verification

✅ Anchor uniqueness asserted **before** writing, scanned **repo-wide over 3648 source files**, each anchor exactly 1 hit, landing sites printed. ⚠️ That was the dispatch's sharpest warning — four near-identical disjunctions is the terrain where one anchor hits three sites — and it was answered with a repo-wide count rather than a local one.

✅ Every ablation proved the mutation on disk **both ways** (injected `new Set([...])` present **and** the removed canonical read absent, counted separately — *"not a bare `git diff --stat`"*). ✅ Restore under a trap whose command is an **absolute-path `cp` from a saved pre-ablation copy** — cwd-independent, today's #5926 lesson — then **`cmp`** to confirm byte-identity, then `git diff HEAD --stat` empty. Three independent restore proofs.

✅ **The contrast held in every leg**: exactly the identity pins red, while the member-set assertion, the restoration probes and the outside-the-family controls stayed green. That is the proof the pin does work the set assertion cannot — and it is what #4580 predicted five sweeps ago.

✅ **The folding measurement bounds the change**: over the whole spec vocabulary plus every alias key, **exactly five inputs land in the family** (`lookup`, `master_detail`, `tree`, `user`, `reference`) — so nothing else widened. ✅ And the live/dead controls (`lookup`/`master_detail`/`user`/`tree` accepted; `reference`/`owner`/nonsense refused identically) are **kept as executable pins so the drop reopens if the spec ever adds the spelling**.

### The #5875 half

✅ **Prose only, and it writes no replacement count** — it points at the census in `expand-fields.ts` instead. That was the instruction most likely to be missed, because "the fourth and last" invites "the seventh and last". ⛔ Writing a new integer would have re-created the defect at a larger size, and the card exists because that has now happened twice.

## ⚠️ Addendum — PR #6064 is RED on CI. Narrow rework in flight; the ACCEPT above stands.

**The review verdict is unchanged.** Every fence held, every measurement re-derived, and the reasoning is accepted as reviewed. What follows is a one-line CI failure and the lesson attached to it — ⛔ not a re-opening of the review.

### The failure

`Type Check` job, at the **`pnpm check:esm-specifiers`** step (`scripts/check-node-esm-load.mjs --specifiers-only`):

```
✗ @object-ui/app-shell: 1 relative specifier(s) without an explicit extension.
  Node's ESM resolver does not extension-search relative specifiers, and this package's
  build emits them unchanged, so its published entry cannot be imported under plain Node.
    packages/app-shell/src/utils/resolveActionParams.ts:36  './paramToField'  →  './paramToField.js'
```

⭐ It is **caused by this PR's own change** — specifically by the good part of it: the `resolveActionParams` face now asks the shared family over the widget key `paramToField` produces, and that new import arrived without the explicit extension this repo's published-ESM rule requires. Fix is `'./paramToField'` → `'./paramToField.js'`, and nothing else.

⚠️ The rework instruction also asks for the gate to be **run**, not just that line patched: the gate stops at the first package, and `@object-ui/plugin-kanban` / `@object-ui/plugin-detail` are also published ESM with new imports from this PR. ⛔ Fixing only the named line and assuming the rest are clean is the wrong shape.

### ⭐ Why this got through — the part worth keeping

This is **not a typo lesson.** The dev's gate set was re-derived by hand from `package.json` and `.github/workflows/`, which is **correct practice in this repo** — objectui has no `scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs`, so there is no canonical list to run. That hand-derived set included `check:phantom-deps`, `check-changeset-*`, `check-control-bytes`, `check-lint-coverage`, `check-type-check-coverage` and `check-package-self-import`.

⛔ It did **not** include `check:esm-specifiers` — because that gate runs **inside the `Type Check` CI job**, under a name that does not look like a type check. A hand-derived set built from top-level script names cannot see it.

**Standing rule for this lane, from here on:**
> ⚠️ **Any PR that adds a new relative import to a published package must run `pnpm check:esm-specifiers`.** And a hand-derived gate set must be checked against the **`Type Check` job's own step list**, not only against the repo's top-level script names — that job runs several `check:*` gates whose names give no hint they live there.

That goes into the seat's standing notes and into every dispatch that touches a published package's imports. ✅ It is also the second time today that this repo's *absence* of a dispatch-gate manifest cost a round-trip — the first being a gate set re-derived correctly but incompletely on #5883. Worth carrying to whoever owns `domain:devx`.

Gate re-read follows the push.
